thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert (P1) triggered for service=redwood-serving-euc1 at 2812346789 - symptoms: 20% 5xx across dedicated pools, ELB target health flapping, DNS slow failover.

mira: seeing 502/504 from customer traffic going to eu-central-1. dashboards show backend packet drops + high ENI detach count.

diego: confirmed. tcp resets on ELB->instance in eu-central-1b, also EBS io timeout errors in cloudwatch for the same AZ.

ashley: customers in EMEA are hitting timeouts, some dedicated clusters are degraded; alerting CS and support.

jonah: route53 health checks for the region look stuck at "healthy" despite backend failures — suspects delayed health propagation.

mira: good catch. can someone check control plane events for EBS detach/attach storms? i see a flurry around 2812346760.

diego: running query now. output snippet:
```
aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=availability-zone,Values=eu-central-1b 
=> ENIs with Status=detached count increased by 37 in last 5m
aws ec2 describe-instances --filters Name=tag:service,Values=redwood-serving-euc1 
=> several instances reporting EBS i/o timeout
```

eva: confirmed EBS io metrics show high latency then timeouts for a subset of volumes. AWS health dashboard shows "degraded" for eu-central-1b EBS control plane.

mira: impact: Hosted API ok (multi-region), but Dedicated pools in eu-central-1 are degraded. customers on reserved capacity are seeing errors. put incident severity to P1. notifying legal/ops.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0458. Channel: #incidents. Runbook: region-eu-network-ebb.

ashley: CS ping: high-value customer A reported 30% failures on requests, they've escalated. Q to oncall: do we failover dedicated pools to eu-west-1?

diego: can do model routing fallback but need to coordinate capacity — eu-west-1 has 60% spare. will kick off partial traffic shift via routing policy.

jonah: warning — route53 TTLs for our weighted records are 60s but health check still showing healthy; if we change weights now might not take immediate effect. suggest creating short-lived alias to endpoint in eu-west-1 and update app routing rules first.

mira: action plan: 1) immediate: shift routing for Dedicated customers with customer-tag=failover to eu-west-1 (soft shift 20% -> 100% over 5m). 2) drain affected targets in eu-central-1. 3) replace instances showing EBS timeout. 4) open support case with AWS for euc1b EBS. 5) notify customers.

diego: executing step 1 now: running infra playbook snippet:
```
# increase weight for eu-west-1 pool
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.example","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-west-1","Weight":80,"AliasTarget":{...}}}]}'
```

jonah: also toggling our internal routing: service-routing -> set fallback_region=euw1 for tag=dedicated-failover

ashley: pinging CS with customer impact template. drafting status page entry.

mira: diego, once weights start moving, run health-checks on eu-west-1 to validate model serving latency and token throughput. we must avoid regression in quality.

diego: health checks green on eu-west-1 for a subset. but embedding latency ~+30ms, generation latency +25ms, acceptable for most. moving to 50% now.

pagerduty-bot: On-call handoff reminder: mira is primary (till 2822340000). Use #incidents for updates.

eva: AWS case opened: case# 1234567890 - EBS control-plane degraded in eu-central-1b, under investigation. AWS referencing internal event id: EBS-EUC1B-2026-03.

jonah: draining targets in eu-central-1b with this command:
```
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:... --targets Id=i-0abc1234
```

mira: quick note: enable circuit breaker on routing rule for any service reporting >20% 5xx for 3m to auto-shift. Config deployed.

diego: shifted to 100% eu-west-1 for tagged customers. metrics show 5xx count dropping for those customers. overall platform 5xx down from 18% -> 6% in 8m.

ashley: status page draft: "We are experiencing elevated 5xx errors for services in eu-central-1. Traffic is being routed to eu-west-1 for affected customers. AWS is investigating an EBS control-plane issue in eu-central-1b. Workaround applied." posting in 2m.

eva: AWS updated case: "We are seeing impact in a subset of Availability Zones and are working to remediate. No ETA provided yet."

diego: starting instance replacements on eu-central-1b: rolling replace group node by node. using snapshot restore for affected volumes where necessary.

mira: coordination note for oncall handoff at 2812346805: diego -> jonah for mitigation ops. diego, please capture next steps and followups.

diego: handoff ack. next steps: 1) continue rolling replacements; 2) validate route53 expiry and revert weights after AWS confirms fix; 3) run postmortem checklist; 4) send targeted customer communications (CS).

jonah: monitoring: set synthetic checks to hit eu-west-1 endpoints for next 24h. added temporary dashboards for dedicated traffic split.

ashley: posted on status page and emailed top-tier customers. copied support playbook and mitigation steps.

incident-bot: Reminder: create incident slack summary and postmortem ticket.

mira: created INC-2026-0458-summary and PM-2026-112 in our tracker. assigning to diego and eva for root cause investigation.

diego: final note before leaving for emergency family errand: if AWS resolves euc1b, we'll gradually shift weights back and monitor for any regression. otherwise keep fallback routing in place for up to 24h. handoff complete. :wave:

jonah: took over ops. continuing monitoring and customer comms. will update here on AWS progress and when weights revert.

ashley: thanks team. prepping postmortem draft template.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0458 escalated -> Major incident status.

jonah: last update at 2812346812: 5xx counts stable at ~4-6%, AWS still investigating. leaving incident open until EBS control plane in euc1b fully resolved.

mira: closing notes: keep this channel as primary. any new customer regressions escalate immediately. great run on mitigation, especially quick routing fallback. :thumbsup:
